title: jscalendar-types omits Eq derive on data structs; jscontact-types derives PartialEq+Eq uniformly — accidental drift, not load-bearing
description:
**Divergence**:
- jscalendar-types: structs from `RecurrenceRule` (src/lib.rs:446) onward derive `PartialEq` but NOT `Eq`. The scalar wrappers `LocalDateTime`/`Duration`/`SignedDuration`/`UTCOffset` derive `Eq`; the larger structs do not.
- jscontact-types: every struct derives `PartialEq, Eq` uniformly (src/lib.rs:152, 199, 231, 264, ...).

**Verification of non-load-bearingness**: the omission of `Eq` in jscalendar is not forced by any field type — none of the affected structs has a `f32`/`f64`, and the shared `extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>` field IS `Eq` (which is why jscontact compiles with `Eq` derived on every extras-bearing struct).

**Caller-observable cost**: callers writing `HashSet<RecurrenceRule>` or using a calendar struct as a `HashMap` key cannot, but callers using analogous contact structs can. Real call sites are uncommon for either, so the practical cost is small.

**Maintainer cost**: a contributor reading both crates side-by-side cannot tell whether the `Eq`-drop in jscalendar is load-bearing or accidental. The answer is "accidental".

**Fix**: add `Eq` to the jscalendar-types data struct derive lists. One-line change per struct. cargo test --workspace should pass unchanged because no current code path depends on the absence.
